builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CTIA-ODE: Continuous-Time Inter-Variable Attention for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
summary: The method replaces discrete-time multivariate forecasting architectures (e.g., Transformer-based or linear channel-mixing models) that require rigid temporal alignment of exogenous variables with a neural-ODE framework in which attention over a static exogenous context is evaluated continuously along the integration path, plus a linear residual anchor and an outlier-robust loss. Costs include ODE-solver compute at training and inference time (which scales with the number of solver steps and can exceed the latency of a single forward pass despite the claimed efficiency), implementation complexity, and dependence on anonymous, non-production code. Failure modes include unstable latent dynamics on noisy or heavy-tailed series despite the dual stabilization, poor transfer when exogenous variables are themselves time-varying or misaligned with the assumed static context, and the general risk that eight-dataset benchmarks do not reflect the reader's domain.
rationale: The approach addresses a real production problem (irregular exogenous alignment) with claims of low memory and latency, but it is an unvalidated research architecture with no quantified gains, so it warrants small-scale benchmarking against simpler baselines rather than adoption.
